sections.h2: What installed base management software keeps
paras: Installed base management software is a register of every unit you have sold and installed, one record per serial number, holding where it is, when it was accepted, what warranty and contract cover it, every service visit since, and any transfer or replacement along the way. In Aura Business this is the Asset and Installed-Base Register in the AMC and Service Contracts suite, and every other suite writes to it: sales adds the unit, service adds the visits, contracts add the cover.

The register matters because it is the AMC pipeline. Every serial whose warranty ends next quarter is a contract to sell; every serial on an expiring AMC is a renewal; every serial with a heavy service history is an upgrade conversation. Without the register those are guesses. With it they are a list with names and dates.

sections.h2: Most dealers know what they sold. Few know what is still running.
sections.lead: The sale is recorded in the invoice. The installation, the acceptance, the moves between wards and the swap under warranty are recorded nowhere.

items.p: The unit was delivered on a challan, installed by an engineer, and accepted by a biomedical officer, and only the challan exists.

items.h: Warranty dates by product, not serial
items.p: Warranty is assumed to be a year from invoice, but the installation was three months later and the claim is refused.
A monitor bought for ICU is now in the emergency ward, and a call from there cannot be matched to the asset.
A unit swapped under warranty starts a new record, and the old one's history and contract are lost.
Nobody can produce the serials whose warranty ends in the next ninety days, so the AMC is sold after the first breakdown.

sections.h2: From delivery to replacement, on one record.

steps.p: The serial on the delivery challan creates the asset against the hospital and location.
The engineer's job card records installation; the customer signs acceptance on the app.
Warranty dates set from acceptance; AMC or CMC attached when sold.
Every PM visit and breakdown call lands in the asset's history.
Transfers between wards, branches or customers recorded with dates.
A replacement serial is linked to the original so cover and history carry across.

items.q: How does a unit get into the installed base?
items.a: When a sales order is delivered, the serial on the delivery challan creates the asset against the customer. The installation job card and the customer's acceptance signature on the app complete the record with the installation date. Existing assets are imported from Excel at setup.

items.q: Can warranty start from installation rather than invoice?
items.a: Yes. Warranty dates on the asset can be set from the acceptance date, the invoice date or a date you enter, so the cover shown on a service call matches what the manufacturer will honour. See warranty management software.

One screen per serial showing its customer and location, warranty and contract status, every service visit with spares and signatures, PM and calibration records, transfers and any linked replacement, plus the documents attached to it.

items.q: How are transfers between hospitals or wards handled?
items.a: An asset transfer records the new location or customer with a date and reason. The history stays on the serial, and contracts can be kept, ended or reassigned depending on the commercial terms.

items.q: Why is the installed base called the AMC pipeline?
items.a: Because every serial with expiring warranty or an expiring AMC is a contract to sell or renew. The register lists them by date with the hospital contact, and the AMC revenue and leakage dashboard shows the rupee value at stake. See the guide.

items.q: Can we track assets we service but did not sell?
items.a: Yes. Assets can be created directly in the register for third-party equipment under your maintenance contracts, with the same history and cover fields as units you sold.
